section: Sky Lab: Observe — Telescope optics lab
changes: Refractor rays focus at an image plane and leave the eyepiece parallel for a relaxed eye
Newtonian rays reflect at a 45-degree secondary before reaching the side image plane
Three selectable light-path stages explain collection, image formation and eyepiece viewing
Exit-beam and 6 mm eye-pupil circles share a calculated size scale
Real lens and mirror telescope presets use published aperture, focal length and eyepiece dimensions
Native optical controls preserve independent values and keyboard focus
A setup preview copies instrument dimensions to the eyepiece field lab while preserving its target and sky settings
Phone layouts keep touch controls and diagram labels readable

data.scope: Rays illustrate one star on the optical axis, with enlarged schematic separations. Numeric optics and common pupil-circle scale are calculated independently. The 6 mm eye pupil is a fixed teaching reference. Gross aperture area omits secondary obstruction, optical losses and eye acceptance. The 2× aperture power guideline is approximate. Lens aberrations, detailed mirror curvature, diffraction and the 90EQ diagonal are omitted.

equations.magnification: objective focal length / eyepiece focal length
equations.secondary: Mirror line y - x = axis - 120; reflected direction exchanges the incident x and y components
